sentences.text: Elornis is an extinct genus of flamingo that lived in the Late Oligocene of Ronzon, France.
Elornis has historically been classified as a member of the Phoenicopteridae, though recent research suggests it may be more basal.

Auguste Aymard first coined the name Elornis in 1855 during a report presented to the Congres Seientifique de France, but his original report only stated that the birds were flamingos without providing a full description or illustrations. Because Aymard's original names were considered nomina nuda, Henri Milne-Edwards is credited as the authority for Elornis, as Aymard's original fossil material was presumed lost, leaving only Milne-Edwards' descriptions and illustrations as available data.
Milne-Edwards described the species Elornis littoralis based on postcranial remains such as the pelvis, tarsometatarsi, tibiotarsi, and furculae.
Lydekker named a fourth species, Elornis (?) anglicus, in 1891, but later research moved this species to the genus Actiornis and identified it as an ibis.
Elornis lived during the Rupelian stage, from 33.9 to 27.3 million years ago.
Research on Elornis is difficult because the current location of the fossil material is unknown, limiting data to Milne-Edwards' descriptions and illustrations.
